Automatic latest models

Opt-in automatic updates for selected model families, bounded catalog polling and historical chat routes.

About 5 min read · 4 sections

On this page
01 Model identity and dates 02 Scope and availability 03 Background checks 04 Verification

Connections offers an Automatic latest models switch and Check now. Enabling it captures the families of the models already selected on this execution host, without changing today's selection. The native fallback selection is captured separately. Turning it off freezes the current selection; it does not bring older versions back or disable an account.

Current selected families + known catalog baseline

Keep old chat routes

Existing chats, explicit model requests and agent profiles keep their exact model and account. An automated update adds a new version-specific alias; it never rebinds an old alias to another model. Older aliases remain routable for saved chats, but their pickerHidden metadata removes them from the normal picker and marks them unchecked in Choose models. Hidden discovery still returns them as hidden. Explicitly selecting an older model makes it visible again and reseeds that provider's watched families and baseline.

The baseline includes models known when the switch was enabled. A model already visible but deliberately left unchecked is not enabled on the next poll. If an initial discovery fails, the first successful discovery establishes its baseline without activating anything. Later failures or empty responses retain the last working selection; they never downgrade a family or switch to another account. Adding a connection while this feature is enabled starts from that connection's chosen models, not every model in its catalog.

Each scope can remember 256 known model IDs. Enabling refuses an oversized baseline rather than silently dropping choices. If a pending scope first sees an oversized baseline, it becomes baselineBlocked and activates nothing, even if the catalog later shrinks. Review the selection and turn the setting off and on to capture a safe baseline again. Catalogs over 4,096 rows are refused whole rather than truncated.

Model identity and dates

The supported families are Astra, Sol, Terra, Luna and Daybreak on GPT routes, and Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku on Claude routes. Copilot's provider-specific IDs are matched within its own account, not against another provider's models. Unknown families, previews and ambiguous variants remain off until explicitly selected. gpt-5.3-codex is not silently renamed to Terra.

Numeric versions decide ordering first: 6.10 is newer than 6.9. For two IDs at the same version, known provider dates can distinguish a newer snapshot only when both dates are available. Missing dates, equal ranks and unclear IDs do not authorize a change. A newer date cannot promote an older numeric version. The gateway never treats first discovery time as a release date.

Model rows show Provider date when available. The official OpenAI model reference defines created as a creation timestamp in Unix seconds, not a release announcement. Creation and first-seen fields are not treated as release dates and do not drive activation. Many subscription catalogs expose no release dates, so version numbers are the reliable fallback. Floating latest IDs such as Daybreak stay under the same ID; the provider can update them without a new alias.

Scope and availability

Only a provider's authenticated, selectable catalog supplies candidates. A missing model is not invented, and a missing login is not repaired by copying credentials from another Mac. M5's pending Copilot login remains a separate setup step. Grok has no verified model-discovery flow and stays pinned to its configured models. Unrecognized local model families likewise stay pinned.

A client-only configuration manages its local native fallback preference, not the remote inference host's providers. An SSH chat uses its execution host's configuration. Native updates write only the gateway's native picker allowlist; they never edit native authentication, model cache or the primary Codex config. New picker reads take the latest valid native presentation settings without changing any loaded chat's model, permissions or routing. An invalid preference file leaves the last valid presentation in place.

Background checks

The existing app-owned gateway service runs metadata maintenance in its process tree every 300 seconds. It never creates a second LaunchAgent or Login Item. Inference servers own a hot-swappable timer; a client-only plan without an inference child runs the timer in its existing supervisor. The settings window does not need to stay open. A fresh process-identity heartbeat reports whether the timer is actually active. It does not restart the service or interrupt work. A slow pass cannot overlap another pass for the same configuration. A toggle or manual edit during discovery makes the outdated result stale rather than overwriting the edit.

There is no guaranteed provider model-release webhook. Five minutes is the poll interval, not a promise of instant visibility; provider propagation, sleep, authentication and native-cache freshness can delay discovery. The native scope uses the public cache maintained by the running native engine. Check now runs the same metadata-only reconciliation; it sends no inference prompt.

gateway auto-latest check --config /absolute/gateway.json
gateway auto-latest status --config /absolute/gateway.json

The app reports when the existing service has not adopted maintenance yet rather than claiming checks are running. Enabling or disabling the policy changes no background registration. A verified legacy 0.8.7 model-maintenance LaunchAgent is removed during migration; foreign jobs are left alone. Output contains fixed outcomes, counts and timestamps, never provider credentials, request bodies, tool arguments or raw failure text.

Configuration stores autoLatestModels.enabled, each provider's selected families and baselineModels, and the separate native scope. Updates use the existing revision guard, private lock, backup and atomic configuration save. The alias ledger continues to reserve retired identities. See connection management and live routing.

Verification

After npm run build, run npm run app:e2e:auto-latest. This private fixture uses a real HTTP gateway with local mock discovery and inference. It verifies unchanged selections at enable, future family upgrades, unrelated models staying off, old aliases remaining routable but hidden, native preference isolation, and disable behavior. It sends no paid inference and changes no installed settings.
